about: In-place binary patches of the repack baseline (AGENTS rule 15). Each entry: rva, length, original_hex (our compile of the original 1.001 source), patched_hex (GAME.EXE), function, what, evidence. Applied after linking in the final build.

entries.what: The repack replaces the validation routine’s 16-byte stack allocation with an immediate true return.
entries.evidence: The recovered C++ accounts for the complete 240-byte COFF contribution. All eleven relocated operands agree with independently resolved bindings. The three contiguous entry bytes are the only differences. See cp69-bindings.json for the whole-function hashes and offsets. Claude integration check 2026-11-25 (level2_check after batch 69, job 1f0418a1): the function differs from GAME.EXE in exactly these bytes and nowhere else; every relocation bound.

entries.what: Archive replaces the call through the cached drive-type import, its result comparison, and the conditional skip with a local constant store and two NOPs.
entries.evidence: Same eight-byte boundary; compiled and image fallback share the imported GetDriveTypeA slot. The next drive-recording block is identical. Claude integration check 2026-11-25 (level2_check after batch 69, job 1f0418a1): the function differs from GAME.EXE in exactly these bytes and nowhere else; every relocation bound.

entries.what: Two NOPs occupy the primary drive loop back edge.
entries.evidence: The preceding increment and compare and the subsequent field reload are intact; the archive does not consume the compare flags. Claude integration check 2026-11-25 (level2_check after batch 69, job 1f0418a1): the function differs from GAME.EXE in exactly these bytes and nowhere else; every relocation bound.

entries.what: The archive changes the post-loop conditional branch to an unconditional branch with its original destination.
entries.evidence: Displacement remains identical; the count test and entire fallback body are still present. Only the opcode differs.
